title: Addicted To
summary: A birthday episode framed by a Silicon Valley cold open and the phrase `addicted to DVDASA`. It moves through anonymous fan art, the K-Town reality series, bodily-fluid pranks, diabetes, wealth, gifts, hoarding, meaning, compulsive viewing, self-harm, turning pain into art, and a long pro-anorexia/pro-bulimia discussion. Every idea remains. The editorial layer rejects four fabricated health-podcast rewrites, protects anonymous/private people, and separates confession from recommendation, performance from fact, and eating-disorder/self-harm material from health guidance.
source_notes: All six cleaner removals are empty zero-duration records. Raw and clean word counts are unchanged.
Four global `health podcast` → `self-description joke` substitutions are rejected. They overwrite literal recurring speech with an invented category.
Dark Dick remains anonymous. Voice, height, ethnic, spouse, restaurant and artist-similarity clues are not reassembled into a legal identity.

NIMH says eating disorders are serious and sometimes fatal, are not a choice, and bulimia can cause reflux, severe dehydration and electrolyte imbalance: https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/eating-disorders

CDC confirms frequent urination and increased hunger can be diabetes symptoms; NIDDK confirms diabetes can contribute to erectile dysfunction. These are risks/symptoms, not certainty about one person: https://www.cdc.gov/diabetes/signs-symptoms/index.html and https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/urologic-diseases/erectile-dysfunction/symptoms-causes
The self-harm, shooting and asphyxiation material is retained as historical ideation/behavior and explicitly not recommended.
Zero diarized turns and zero identity windows mean no dialogue is assigned to named speakers.
Forty-two narrow spans protect anonymous creators, private partners, twins, relatives, coworkers, fans, messages, residences, venues, health and financial details without deleting ideas.
speaker_policy: Names in the editorial layer identify explicitly introduced public participants, works and contextual references only. Zero turns and zero voice windows cannot support named transcript dialogue.

connections.why: The cold open turns Choe's public Facebook-stock story and controversy into fictional dialogue.
A recurring participant asks that others not use his headphones/station when absent.
Dark Dick's public work is celebrated while the show repeatedly tries to infer his identity.
Frequent urination, hunger and ED are real possible symptoms/complications but not certainties.
Meticulous sanitation coexists with stories of alcohol-related loss of control.
Approachability and a joking pass do not authorize touching or climbing on someone.
The cast sees the reality series as both addictive and degrading representation.
A participant explicitly says he is addicted to DVDASA and binges its surrounding ecosystem.
The show's old category ranking is a joke/identity, not medical accreditation.
An assistant represents the artist on a card call, exposing impersonation and account-boundary risk.
Handmade gifts matter more than purchasable luxury to someone who can buy objects.
Gratitude for handmade work coexists with storage, obligation and inability to discard.
Birthday avoidance is linked to attention, disappointment and feeling undeserving.
A gold chain and luxury vehicles are framed as loss targets rather than security.
Refusal to discard objects contradicts the stated readiness to walk away from anything.
The episode's philosophical center joins intense care with radical impermanence.
Reality actors and DVDASA participants are described as heightened versions of themselves.
Provocation creates discussion but does not make all statements fictional or literal.
Listening, watching, commenting and masturbating fold the audience into the show's world.
A private partner becomes recognizable from relationship context despite never appearing.
Cutting and self-punching are described as attempts to feel and make material.
Public film footage documents self-injury while also turning it into an aesthetic object.
Shooting oneself for art is historical ideation, not a completed act or instruction.
A therapist's reported interpretation connects provocative disclosure to cutting/shooting metaphors.
The creative thesis preserves transformation without making injury necessary for creativity.
The speaker treats lack of expertise as a prompt for explanation, not as expertise itself.
Pro-ana/pro-mia communities turn starvation, purging and shame into techniques.
A large private meal is followed by forced vomiting, pain, reflux and renewed temptation.
Chew-and-spit behavior is presented as food control but is not diabetes care.
The episode closes with `never stop` after framing the show as both gift and verbal self-harm.
